Subject: ZenPay benchmarking: throughput & latency acceptance criteria

Hi Olivia,

Nice to meet you — thanks for the quick intro last week. Per our onboarding checklist I wanted to put the acceptance criteria and a proposed load test plan on paper so we have a clear handoff from CS to Eng for the implementation and benchmarking runs.

High-level acceptance targets (proposed):
- Baseline (normal traffic mix): p95 latency <= 180 ms for 512-token requests
- Sustained throughput: 120 requests/sec with p95 <= 200 ms
- Spike tolerance: brief spikes to ~300 req/sec without error-rate > 1% (for up to 60s)

Planned test environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) in us-west-2
- Continuous batching enabled; KV prefix caching will be on for warm runs
- Test model: open-llama-16k-quant (we will validate model variant during baseline)

Proposed run cadence:
1) Baseline ramp (10 -> 120 req/s over 10m)
2) Sustained 45m at 120 req/s while collecting p50/p95/p99, GPU util, and per-token cost
3) Two spike bursts (60s each) at 300 req/s to validate graceful degradation/fallbacks

I've attached a short plan (zenpay-benchmark-plan-20260804.pdf) and a YAML test profile we can execute. Can you confirm: (a) the traffic mix you want us to approximate (chat vs. single-turn generation), and (b) preferred test windows (UTC) for the Dedicated pool?

Once you confirm, I'll loop in Dev and Monica to finalize the test harness and schedule the runs.

Thanks,

Hi Olivia and team,

Thanks for the traffic breakdown — that helps. We've scheduled the first baseline run for Fri Aug 6, 02:30–04:30 PDT (02:30 start to allow warm-up). Plan summary and acceptance checklist below:

Run plan:
- 02:30–02:40: warm-up traffic (cache priming)
- 02:40–03:25: steady 120 rps (mixed traffic per your distribution)
- 03:25–03:35: spike 300 rps (60s), recover 3m
- 03:40–04:10: extended steady 120 rps (observability window)

Acceptance checklist (pass = all true):
- p95 latency <= 200 ms for 512-token multi-turn samples
- Error rate < 1% during steady period
- Token throughput >= expected (per-request token counts) and stable GPU util (no sustained >95% GPU saturation)
- No unexplained queue spikes or tail latency degradations in traces
I'll attach the short run playbook and will publish result links to the shared Drive after the run. If we see borderline results we'll immediately run a blocking spike test and produce a remediation plan (config tweaks, autoscale bump, or model variant fallback).

Subject: Re: ZenPay benchmarking: throughput & latency acceptance criteria — results summary

Hi all,

We completed the baseline and spike runs this morning. Summary highlights (full CSV and GPU profiles attached):

Baseline steady 120 rps (mixed traffic):
- Observed p50/p95/p99 for 512-token samples: 45 ms / 172 ms / 380 ms
- Error rate: 0.4% (mostly transient 429s during a single 12s burst)
- GPU util: 62–78% during steady state; occasional momentary micro-bursts to 88% during 3rd minute of a spike

Spike tests (300 rps, 60s bursts):
- System handled 300 rps but we observed elevated queue wait times and a short period (approx 8–12s) where 429s increased to ~3.5% during immediate post-spike recovery
- No model crashes; fallback routing engaged for a handful of requests as configured

Notes and recommendations:
- Pass vs targets: the run meets the proposed acceptance targets for steady-state p95 and sustained throughput.
- Action items: recommend a small autoscale headroom increase for Dedicated by 10% and a conservative tokenization pre-warm for heavy multi-turn sessions to reduce tail spikes.

Attachments: zenpay-load-results-20260806.csv (text/csv), zenpay-gpu-profiles-20260806.pdf (application/pdf)

I can host a 30-min review with SREs to walk the CSV and traces — propose today at 16:30 PDT if that works for ZenPay.

Thanks,
Monica
